question: What dated reef-fish evidence is available for Ticao Island, Masbate, and can it support a named species list or fishery map?

sourcesReviewed.title: Fish Standing Stock and Catch from Coral Reefs in Three Regions of the Philippines
sourcesReviewed.provider: Silliman Journal / Silliman University Institute of Environmental and Marine Sciences
sourcesReviewed.citation: Utzurrum, J. A. T., Reboton, C. T., & Calumpong, H. P. (2016). Fish Standing Stock and Catch from Coral Reefs in Three Regions of the Philippines. Silliman Journal, 57(2), 17-40.
sourcesReviewed.access: Official bound issue PDF and Silliman Journal OJS page reviewed. The PDF copyright page says all rights reserved and requires written permission for reproduction.

sourcesReviewed.title: Assessment on the Coral and Reef Fish Communities in Ticao Island, Masbate
sourcesReviewed.citation: Reboton, C. T., & Candido, A. (2014). Assessment on the Coral and Reef Fish Communities in Ticao Island, Masbate. Ecology, Environment & Conservation, 19 (Special Issue on Coastal Resource Management), 33-43.
sourcesReviewed.access: Publisher abstract page only; the site advertises the full article at USD 20 for international subscribers. No purchase or request was made.

reefSites.name: Baladingan reef, Sitio Baladingan, Barangay Famosa, Monreal, Ticao Island
Tacdugan reef, Barangay Tacdugan, San Jacinto, Ticao Island

studyScopeAsReported.fishVisualCensusAsReported: Three 50-m transects per site; fish within 5 m on each side of the transect were identified, counted and size-estimated. The article says fish identification used an Allen et al. field guide and FishBase 2014.
studyScopeAsReported.catchMonitoringAsReported: A separate roving-creel survey monitored five landing sites. Famosa was monitored for 46 days over June-December 2013; the article says most Famosa landings came from coastal waters of Famosa and Tacdugan. No catch monitoring was available for Tacdugan as a separate landing site.
studyScopeAsReported.related2014Abstract: Reboton and Candido's abstract reports a 100-ha patchy reef in Barangay Famosa, 69 reef-fish species and 24 target species. The full article and species list were not inspected; this count is a distinct source claim, not a correction or confirmation of the 2013 survey counts.

evidenceBoundary: The 2013 paper gives site-level species richness totals, not a species-by-site list in the inspected results. No names can be derived from a count.
Coordinates are point/range descriptions of field sites and transect localities, not reef polygons, administrative boundaries or safe fishing zones.
Landing-site catch records cover nearby coastal fishing waters, not a demonstrated capture point at either mapped reef transect.
Both studies are historical. Neither establishes current presence, current abundance, legal fishing access or safety.
The 2016 Silliman issue says all rights reserved and requires written permission. The full 2014 paper was paywalled and no separate license was verified.

disposition.reason: The accessible sources provide dated site-level richness, but not a reusable named list or exact catch-to-reef crosswalk; rights are restrictive or unresolved.

nextAction: Seek written permission and a species-by-site taxon table or field log from the Silliman University team for the 2013 census; request an author-accessible copy of the 2014 baseline without paying or sending a request automatically. Continue separate Masbate mangrove, estuary, reef and inland-water coverage.
